quality_guards: COSHH covers many hazardous substances but lead, asbestos and radioactive substances remain under separate regimes.
Absence of a Workplace Exposure Limit is not evidence that a substance is safe.
COSHH Essentials is generic guidance and does not replace a suitable and sufficient task-specific assessment.
Noise action and limit values are occupational daily, weekly or peak exposure measures rather than environmental nuisance thresholds.
Hearing protection supplements feasible source, engineering and organisational controls.
Hand-arm and whole-body vibration use different exposure action and limit values.
Weekly averaging of vibration exposure is available only in limited circumstances and does not remove ALARP duties.
Vibration calculators depend on representative magnitude and duration inputs.
Welding RPE selection depends on task duration, face fit, wearer and contaminant; particulate filters do not cover every gas.
LEV testing and records demonstrate control maintenance but do not prove zero exposure.
Waste fire-prevention guidance has waste-stream and activity exclusions that require site-specific applicability checks.
Waste permits, records and fire plans are operator-, site- and time-specific.
MOT history does not prove current vehicle condition and recall status changes after manufacturer or repair updates.
Priority Services Register support does not guarantee uninterrupted supply or a fixed restoration time.
Workplace, waste, vehicle and energy service evidence is not converted into exact parcel-level probability.
Live 130-candidate/16-endpoint parity, browser DOM/console acceptance and publisher remote readback remain required.
